Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring adoption of core competencies for early care and education professionals.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to adopting core competencies for early care andeducation professionals; adding a new section to chapter 43.215 RCW;and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that adoptingstatewide core competencies for early care and education professionalsis important because the competencies: (1) Define what early care and education professionals need to knowand be able to do to provide quality care and education for children; (2) Serve as the foundation for decisions and practices carried outby professionals in all early care and education settings; (3) Establish a set of standards for early care and educationsettings that support the professionalism for the field; and (4) Are an integral part of a comprehensive professionaldevelopment system.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.215 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: By December 31, 2011, the department shall adopt core competencies p. 1 SB 5715for early care and education professionals and develop animplementation plan. The department shall incorporate the corecompetencies into all appropriate professional developmentopportunities including, but not limited to, the quality rating andimprovement system, the early childhood education and assistanceprogram, and the early support for infants and toddlers program. Thepurpose of the core competencies is to serve as a foundation for whatearly care and education professionals need to know and do to providequality care for children. The core competencies must be reviewed andupdated every five years.
